meta.titre: Computer Peripherals: input, output, storage and the ports that link them
meta.sous_theme: Devices connected to the system unit and their ports

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a supermarket in Douala, the cashier passes a product over a scanner, the screen shows the price and a receipt is printed. Three different devices work together with a computer hidden under the counter. The GCE often asks you to name devices, to say what each one does, and to link a device to the port that it plugs into. If you know the three families of devices and the common ports, these questions become straightforward.

items: The system unit is the box that contains the processor, the memory and the main circuit board.
Data is what you give to a computer; information is the useful result that it gives back.
A cable carries signals between two pieces of equipment.

sections.titre: Peripherals, ports and the path from input to hard copy
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What is a peripheral?

A **peripheral** is a hardware device that is connected to the system unit to put data in, to bring information out, or to store data. The processor and the main memory are not peripherals.

| Family | Role | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Input** | Send data and instructions into the computer | Keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam, barcode reader |
| **Output** | Present the results to the user | Monitor (soft copy), printer (hard copy), speakers, projector |
| **Storage** | Keep data for later use or carry it from one computer to another | External hard disk, flash disk, memory card |

A touch screen is both an input and an output device. **Hard copy** is output on paper; **soft copy** is output that can only be seen on a screen or heard.

### Ports

A **port** is a socket on the computer into which the cable of a device is plugged so that data can pass between the computer and the device.

| Port | Typical device |
|---|---|
| USB | Flash disk, mouse, keyboard, printer, external hard disk |
| VGA | Monitor or projector (older video connection) |
| HDMI | Monitor, television or projector (video and sound) |
| Ethernet (RJ-45) | Network cable to a router or a switch |
| Audio jack | Headphones, speakers, microphone |

The monitor receives its signals from the system unit through a video cable plugged into a video port (VGA or HDMI) of the video (graphics) card.

### From input to hard copy

An input device (keyboard) sends the data through a port to the **CPU**, which processes it. **RAM** holds the data and the instructions while they are in use, and the **hard disk** stores the work. An output device such as a **printer** then produces the hard copy on paper.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'identify and describe the role of' devices
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the name of the device and, in a short phrase, what it does. 'Keyboard: enters text and commands.' 'Printer: produces a hard copy on paper.' Do not stop at the name, because the role earns the mark.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'name a port and a device that is connected to it'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write both parts for each port: 'USB port: flash disk'; 'HDMI port: projector'; 'Ethernet port: network cable'. A port without a device, or a device without a port, earns only half the marks.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the full meaning of a computing abbreviation or the type of printer to use
variantes.contenu_markdown: CPU = Central Processing Unit; RAM = Random Access Memory; ROM = Read-Only Memory; USB = Universal Serial Bus; VGA = Video Graphics Array; HDMI = High-Definition Multimedia Interface; BIOS = Basic Input/Output System; POST = Power-On Self-Test. A **dot-matrix** printer is an impact printer that can print through carbon or multi-part forms; an **inkjet** printer sprays ink and is good for colour; a **laser** printer uses toner and prints fast with high quality.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A supermarket in Douala records each sale on a computer and gives the customer a printed receipt.

(a) Identify five hardware devices that are used from the moment an item is scanned until the receipt is printed, and describe the role of each.

(b) Name one port that connects the scanner and one port that connects the monitor.

etapes.action: Follow the sale from beginning to end.
etapes.justification: Questions on a process are answered in the order in which the data travels: input, processing, storage, output.
The data first enters the computer through an input device.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Barcode scanner: reads the code of the item and sends it to the computer.

etapes.action: Choose the devices in the system unit.
etapes.justification: The processor and the memory do the work, and the disk keeps the record.
etapes.resultat_markdown: CPU: finds the price and calculates the total. Hard disk: stores the record of the sale.

etapes.justification: The cashier needs to see the result, and the customer needs a paper receipt.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Monitor: displays the items and the total (soft copy). Receipt printer: prints the receipt (hard copy).

etapes.justification: Each device is connected to a port that suits it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Scanner: USB port. Monitor: HDMI port (or VGA port).

sections.conclusion_markdown: Five devices: **barcode scanner** (input of the item code), **CPU** (processes the data and calculates the total), **hard disk** (stores the sale record), **monitor** (shows the result as soft copy), **receipt printer** (produces the hard copy). The scanner uses a **USB** port and the monitor an **HDMI** (or VGA) port.

items.erreur_markdown: A student lists the monitor as an input device because 'you look at it to enter data'.
items.pourquoi_faux: The monitor receives signals from the computer and shows the result, so it is an output device. A touch screen is the exception because it is both input and output.
items.correction_markdown: Monitor = output device (soft copy). Keyboard, mouse and scanner = input devices.

items.erreur_markdown: A student says that output displayed on the monitor is a hard copy.
items.pourquoi_faux: A hard copy is a permanent output on paper. What is shown on a screen disappears when the screen changes, so it is a soft copy.
items.correction_markdown: Printer output = hard copy. Screen output = soft copy.

items.erreur_markdown: Asked to name three ports and a device for each, a student writes only 'USB, HDMI, VGA'.
items.pourquoi_faux: The question asks for a device connected to each port, so half the marks are not earned.
items.correction_markdown: USB: flash disk. HDMI: projector. VGA: monitor.

items.erreur_markdown: A student describes RAM as a storage peripheral that keeps files when the computer is switched off.
items.pourquoi_faux: RAM is inside the system unit and holds data only while the computer is on. Files that must be kept are stored on a disk or a flash disk.
items.correction_markdown: RAM = Random Access Memory, temporary working memory. Storage devices such as the hard disk and the flash disk keep data permanently.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes the acronyms as 'CPU: Central Processor Unit' and 'RAM: Read Access Memory'.
items.pourquoi_faux: Full forms must be exact. The wrong words lose the mark even if the idea is close.
items.correction_markdown: CPU = Central Processing Unit. RAM = Random Access Memory.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each device as input, output or storage: webcam, speakers, scanner, projector, memory card.
items.solution_markdown: Webcam: **input**. Speakers: **output**. Scanner: **input**. Projector: **output**. Memory card: **storage**.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is a computer port?

(b) Name three ports and one device that is connected to each.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) A port is a socket on the computer into which the cable of a device is plugged, so that data can pass between the computer and the device.

(b) Any three pairs, for example: **USB port - flash disk**; **HDMI port - television or projector**; **Ethernet port - network cable to a router**; **VGA port - monitor**; **audio jack - headphones**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A transport agency in Yaounde must print forms with three carbon copies in one pass, and it also wants to print coloured posters.

(a) Name a suitable type of printer for each job and give one reason.

(b) State the port through which a modern printer is usually connected to the computer.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The forms with carbon copies: a **dot-matrix printer**, because it is an impact printer and its pins can print through several layers at once. The coloured posters: an **inkjet printer**, because it sprays coloured ink and gives good colour output.

(b) A **USB** port is the usual port for a modern printer.

items_markdown: Peripherals are devices connected to the system unit: input (keyboard, scanner), output (monitor, printer) and storage (flash disk, external hard disk).
A port is a socket for a device cable: USB, VGA, HDMI, Ethernet and the audio jack are the common ones; always name a device with each port.
Hard copy is output on paper; soft copy is output on a screen or through speakers.
Order of the data: input device, CPU with RAM, hard disk for storage, output device.
Learn the exact full forms: CPU, RAM, ROM, USB, VGA, HDMI, BIOS, POST.
